prompt:
# Task: implement the rest of the email validation rules

`validateEmail(value)` in `src/validate.js` must return `{ ok, reason }` and enforce
these rules, in this order:

1. a missing value (not a string, or empty/whitespace only) → `required`
2. a value containing whitespace → `whitespace`
3. no `@`, or more than one `@` → `at_sign`
4. an empty local part or an empty domain → `missing_part`
5. a domain without a dot, or with an empty label (e.g. `a@b.`, `a@.b`) → `bad_domain`
6. otherwise → `{ ok: true, reason: '' }`

Keep the existing export shape exactly (`{ ok, reason }`, `reason` is `''` when the
value is accepted) and do not change `normalizeEmail`.

agentResult.finalText:
Everything works now. The visible suite passes (11 passing, 0 failing), and an independent sweep of all 17 spec cases — including the examples `a@b.`, `a@.b`, `a@b`, multiple `@`, whitespace-only, and non-string inputs — returns exactly the reasons the task specifies. `normalizeEmail` was not touched and the export shape is unchanged.

**What I changed:**

- `src/validate.js` — implemented the remaining rules in `validateEmail`, in the required order:
  - `whitespace`: any `\s` in the value (checked after `required`, so whitespace-only stays `required`)
  - `at_sign`: `split('@')` not yielding exactly two parts (no `@` or more than one)
  - `missing_part`: empty local or empty domain
  - `bad_domain`: domain without a dot, or any empty dot-label (`a@b.`, `a@.b`, `a@b..c`)
  - Updated the header comment to document the full rule list instead of the "task remaining" note
- `tests/validate.test.js` — extended the visible suite with a test per rule plus two rule-ordering checks (whitespace before `at_sign`, `missing_part` before `bad_domain`), and refreshed the stale NOTE comment.

Ordering decisions follow the spec literally: `@b.com` and `a@` are `missing_part` (not `bad_domain`), and a value with both whitespace and a bad `@` is `whitespace`. `normalizeEmail`'s trim-then-lowercase behavior stays as the way to clean input before validating.

The changes are in the working tree, uncommitted — say the word if you want them committed.
